subject: Psychiatry
title: Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar Mood Disorders
preview: Separate major depressive episodes from mania/hypomania and remember the safety considerations of lithium therapy.

sections.title: Depression: the clinical syndrome
points: Look for persistent depressed mood or anhedonia alongside sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, guilt and suicide-related symptoms.
Evaluate medical, substance-related and medication contributors and assess safety.

sections.title: Bipolar differential and medication safety
points: Mania includes a distinct period of elevated or irritable mood with increased energy, altered sleep and changes in judgment or behavior.
Lithium clearance is sensitive to renal function, dehydration and interacting drugs such as selected diuretics and NSAIDs.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: A patient presenting with depression may have a past history of hypomania or mania, affecting treatment decisions.
Do not assume a single lithium therapeutic concentration range is suitable for every patient or laboratory.

quickRevision: Major depression combines a sustained cluster of mood, interest, energy, cognitive and vegetative symptoms with functional impact.
Bipolar I disorder requires a history of mania; screening for past mania is essential before treating depressive symptoms.
Lithium needs kidney, thyroid, interactions and concentration monitoring because toxicity risk changes with hydration and renal function.

quiz.question: Which symptom distinguishes mania from unipolar major depressive disorder?
options: A distinct episode of elevated or irritable mood with increased energy
quiz.explanation: A distinct episode of elevated or irritable mood with increased energy. Mania includes a distinct period of elevated or irritable mood with increased energy, altered sleep and changes in judgment or behavior.
